chapters.chapter_title: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates

question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Cartesian Coordinate Fundamentals & Distance Formula

questions.question_text: What are the coordinates of the origin where the x-axis and y-axis intersect on a Cartesian plane?
A point P has an abscissa of -4 and an ordinate of 3. In which quadrant does P lie?
Find the perpendicular distance of the point A(-6, 8) from (i) the x-axis and (ii) the y-axis.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(i) Perpendicular distance from x-axis is |y| = |8| = 8 units.
(ii) Perpendicular distance from y-axis is |x| = |-6| = 6 units.

questions.question_text: Using the Baudhāyana-Pythagoras distance formula, calculate the distance between P(2, 3) and Q(10, 9).
Find the reflection of the point B(4, -5) across (i) the x-axis, (ii) the y-axis, and (iii) the origin.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(i) Reflection across x-axis negates y: (4, 5).
(ii) Reflection across y-axis negates x: (-4, -5).
(iii) Reflection across origin negates both: (-4, 5).

questions.question_text: Show algebraically using the distance formula that the points A(1, 1), B(4, 5), and C(1, 5) form a right-angled triangle on the Cartesian plane, and compute its area.

A delivery drone operates on a 2D grid city layout. Base station is at O(0,0). Drone delivers to house A(3, 4) and then house B(9, 12).
(i) What is the direct distance from base station to House A? (2 Marks)
(ii) What is the straight-line distance between House A and House B? (2 Marks)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(i) Distance OA = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = sqrt(25) = 5 km.
(ii) Distance AB = sqrt((9-3)^2 + (12-4)^2) = sqrt(6^2 + 8^2) = sqrt(100) = 10 km.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 2 - Midpoint, Trisection & Geometric Transformations

questions.question_text: Any point lying on the y-axis has coordinates of the form:
The sign convention of coordinates in Quadrant IV is:
Find the coordinates of the midpoint of line segment joining A(-4, 6) and B(8, -2).
If the distance between P(x, -1) and Q(3, 2) is 5 units, find all possible values of x.
Find the points of trisection P and Q of the line segment joining A(2, -2) and B(-7, 4).
Prove that the points A(2, -2), B(14, 10), C(11, 13), and D(-1, 1) form a rectangle on the Cartesian plane.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Calculate side lengths: AB = sqrt(12^2 + 12^2) = sqrt(288); CD = sqrt((-12)^2 + (-12)^2) = sqrt(288).
2. BC = sqrt((-3)^2 + 3^2) = sqrt(18); AD = sqrt((-3)^2 + 3^2) = sqrt(18).
3. Opposite sides equal: AB = CD and BC = AD.
4. Diagonal AC = sqrt(9^2 + 15^2) = sqrt(81 + 225) = sqrt(306).
5. Diagonal BD = sqrt((-15)^2 + (-9)^2) = sqrt(306). Equal diagonals confirm rectangle.

questions.question_text:
An architect is planning a square park ABCD on a grid. A is at (0,0), B is at (6,0), C is at (6,6), and D is at (0,6).
(i) Calculate the length of the diagonal AC. (2 Marks)
(ii) Find the coordinates of the central fountain located at the intersection of diagonals AC and BD. (2 Marks)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(i) Diagonal AC = sqrt((6-0)^2 + (6-0)^2) = sqrt(36 + 36) = sqrt(72) = 6*sqrt(2) units.
(ii) Center is midpoint of AC = ((0+6)/2, (0+6)/2) = (3, 3).

question_papers.paper_title: Set 3 - Historical Roots & Coordinate Applications

questions.question_text: In ancient Indian altar geometry (Śhulbasūtras), what term referred to the east-west reference axis?
If a point lies in Quadrant III, the signs of its (abscissa, ordinate) are:
Find the point on the x-axis which is equidistant from (2, -5) and (-2, 9).
State the distance of point P(-3, -4) from the origin O(0,0).
Plot vertices A(0, 4), B(-3, 0), C(0, -4), and D(3, 0) on a Cartesian grid. Name the quadrilateral ABCD and calculate its perimeter.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
All 4 sides equal: AB = BC = CD = DA = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = 5 units.
Diagonals AC = 8 (vertical) and BD = 6 (horizontal) are perpendicular.
Quadrilateral is a Rhombus. Perimeter = 4 * 5 = 20 units.

questions.question_text: Three vertices of a parallelogram ABCD are A(-2, 1), B(1, 0), and C(4, 3). Find the coordinates of the fourth vertex D.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
In a parallelogram, diagonals AC and BD bisect each other.
Midpoint of AC = ((-2+4)/2, (1+3)/2) = (1, 2).
Let D = (x, y). Midpoint of BD = ((1+x)/2, (0+y)/2).
Equating midpoints: (1+x)/2 = 1 => x = 1; (0+y)/2 = 2 => y = 4.
Fourth vertex D is (1, 4).

questions.question_text:
Urban planners in Harappa laid out main roads along orthogonal axes intersecting at right angles.
(i) Explain how town layout aligns with Cartesian axes. (2 Marks)
(ii) If a grain store is at (5, 12) and town gate is at (0,0), find the direct access road length. (2 Marks)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(i) Two perpendicular main avenues act as x and y axes dividing town into 4 blocks/quadrants, enabling unique street grid coordinates.
(ii) Distance = sqrt(5^2 + 12^2) = sqrt(25 + 144) = sqrt(169) = 13 units.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 4 - Collinearity & Advanced Coordinate Geometry

questions.question_text: The distance between points (a, 0) and (0, b) is given by:
If (x, y) = (-y, x), then x and y must be:
Check whether points A(1, 5), B(2, 3), and C(-2, -11) are collinear using distance formula.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
AB = sqrt(1^2 + (-2)^2) = sqrt(5).
BC = sqrt((-4)^2 + (-14)^2) = sqrt(16 + 196) = sqrt(212) = 2*sqrt(53).
AC = sqrt((-3)^2 + (-16)^2) = sqrt(9 + 256) = sqrt(265).
Since AB + BC != AC, points are NOT collinear.

questions.question_text: Find the point on the y-axis which is equidistant from A(6, 5) and B(-4, 3).
Show that the points A(3, 0), B(6, 4), and C(-1, 3) are the vertices of a right-angled isosceles triangle.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
AB = sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = 5.
BC = sqrt((-7)^2 + (-1)^2) = sqrt(50) = 5*sqrt(2).
AC = sqrt((-4)^2 + 3^2) = 5.
AB = AC = 5 (Isosceles). AB^2 + AC^2 = 25 + 25 = 50 = BC^2 (Right angled at A).

questions.question_text: Find the centre and radius of a circle passing through points A(0,0), B(4,0), and C(0,6).
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Since angle A = 90 degrees (formed by axes at origin), BC is the diameter of the circumcircle.
Centre O' is midpoint of BC = ((4+0)/2, (0+6)/2) = (2, 3).
Radius r = 1/2 * BC = 1/2 * sqrt(4^2 + 6^2) = 1/2 * sqrt(52) = sqrt(13) units.

questions.question_text: If A(1, 2), B(4, y), C(x, 6), and D(3, 5) are vertices of a parallelogram in order, find x and y.
Prove that points A(-2, -1), B(1, 0), C(4, 3), and D(1, 2) form a parallelogram.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
AB = sqrt(3^2 + 1^2) = sqrt(10); CD = sqrt((-3)^2 + (-1)^2) = sqrt(10).
BC = sqrt(3^2 + 3^2) = sqrt(18); AD = sqrt(3^2 + 3^2) = sqrt(18).
Opposite sides equal => ABCD is a parallelogram.

questions.question_text: Find the coordinates of the circumcentre of triangle with vertices A(3, 0), B(0, 4), and C(0, 0), and calculate circumradius.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Triangle is right-angled at C(0,0). Circumcentre is midpoint of hypotenuse AB.
Circumcentre O' = ((3+0)/2, (0+4)/2) = (1.5, 2).
Circumradius R = 1/2 * AB = 1/2 * sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = 2.5 units.

questions.marking_scheme_answer: Parallel line has same slope a = 4. Equation y = 4x + b. Substitute (1,8): 8 = 4(1) + b => b = 4. Equation is y = 4x + 4.

questions.question_text: Verify whether x = 4 is a zero of polynomial p(x) = 3x - 12.

Determine slope and intercepts for lines L1: 2x - 3y = 6 and L2: 4x - 6y = 12. Are these lines intersecting, parallel, or coincident?
questions.marking_scheme_answer:

L2: y = (4/6)x - 2 => y = (2/3)x - 2 (Slope 2/3, y-intercept -2).
Since slopes and y-intercepts are identical, lines L1 and L2 are COINCIDENT (infinite intersections).

questions.marking_scheme_answer:

question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Real Number Hierarchy & Decimal Expansions

questions.question_text: Which of the following numbers is an irrational number?
A rational number p/q has a terminating decimal expansion if denominator q has prime factors:
Insert two rational numbers between 1/3 and 1/2.
Convert recurring decimal x = 0.666... into a fraction in p/q form.
Convert 0.2353535... into a rational number in simplest p/q form.
Prove by contradiction that sqrt(2) is an irrational number.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Assume sqrt(2) = p/q where gcd(p,q)=1.
2. 2 = p^2/q^2 => p^2 = 2q^2 => p is even (p=2k).
3. (2k)^2 = 2q^2 => 4k^2 = 2q^2 => q^2 = 2k^2 => q is even.
4. Both p and q even contradicts gcd(p,q)=1.
5. Therefore sqrt(2) is irrational.

questions.question_text:
Mādhava of Saṅgamagrāma derived pi/4 = 1 - 1/3 + 1/5 - 1/7 + ...
(i) Why are finite partial sums strictly rational? (2 Marks)
(ii) Calculate 3rd partial sum S3. (2 Marks)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(i) Sum of finite rational fractions is rational, whereas pi is irrational.
(ii) S3 = 1 - 1/3 + 1/5 = 15/15 - 5/15 + 3/15 = 13/15.

questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(i) 3 (Rational).
(ii) 2*pi (Irrational, product of non-zero rational and irrational).

questions.question_text: Explain how to construct sqrt(2) on a number line using a right triangle.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Draw right triangle at origin with base = 1 unit and height = 1 unit. Hypotenuse = sqrt(1^2 + 1^2) = sqrt(2). Swing arc with compass from origin to cut number line at sqrt(2).

questions.question_text: Describe the construction steps for generating the Square Root Spiral (Wheel of Theodorus) up to sqrt(4).
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Start with right triangle T1 with legs 1 and 1 => hypotenuse sqrt(2).
2. Build T2 on hypotenuse sqrt(2) with perpendicular leg 1 => hypotenuse sqrt(3).
3. Build T3 on hypotenuse sqrt(3) with perpendicular leg 1 => hypotenuse sqrt(4) = 2.

questions.question_text: Prove that 3 + 2*sqrt(5) is an irrational number, given that sqrt(5) is irrational.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Assume r = 3 + 2*sqrt(5) is rational p/q.
2. 2*sqrt(5) = r - 3 => sqrt(5) = (r - 3)/2.
3. Since r is rational, (r - 3)/2 is rational.
4. This implies sqrt(5) is rational, contradicting given fact.
5. Thus 3 + 2*sqrt(5) is irrational.

questions.question_text:

questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(i) Periodicity is 6 digits (142857).
(ii) 3/7 = 3 * 0.142857... Cyclic rotation starting at digit 4 gives 0.428571428571...

(ii) Denominator prime factors must be powers of 2 only.

questions.question_text: Prove that the sum of opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral is 180 degrees.
